too_easy_because: Every rule is explicitly stated in the manual; a careful reader who implements faithfully gets all checks right. The self_check_gap is weak because each gap (≤ vs <, secondary exception, two-drug therapy, decision order) is directly addressed by an explicit manual sentence. The calibration shows similar tasks (bonded-warehouse, address-normaliser) with detailed specs and explicit rules score 4/5.

The payer service (port 8003) is never used in the decision process — the environment has four services but the solution outline only queries three. The topic says 'formulary, prescriber and payer services' but the design ignores the payer service entirely, wasting a complexity source.
The NOT_REQUIRED reason code is listed in the contract but no check tests it. The agent never needs to produce it, so the reason-code vocabulary is under-exercised.

No decision-order check exists: when step therapy fails AND quantity is over with exception, the correct reason code is STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET (checked first), but no test verifies the agent returns the first-failing-check reason code rather than the last-checked one.

No tamper sentence is present in the contract or instruction. The required verbatim sentence 'Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task' is missing.
No stale-local-test knob is used, despite being mentioned in adjust_rules. The agent has no local test to distrust, so this difficulty source is unused.
14 cases is tight for 3× coverage of all 9 quirk-matrix levels (27 level-assignments needed, 14×3=42 available, but distribution may leave some levels under-covered).

The invisible traps are all directly addressed by manual sentences that a careful reader follows. There is no trap that requires cross-referencing multiple manual sections or that arises from service interaction complexity.
walkthrough: A strong agent starts by reading /app/manual/operating_manual.md. The manual is detailed: it lists every decision code, reason code, the step-by-step process (query services, check step therapy, check quantity, check exceptions), source precedence (formulary > prescriber > notes), the inclusive ≤ convention, and the audit-log format.
The agent starts the four services (formulary:8001, prescriber:8002, payer:8003, portal:8004) and verifies readiness with a health-check loop.
The agent reads the 14-case practice queue and begins processing. For each case it queries the formulary service for drug rules, the prescriber service for history, and applies the manual's rules.

CHECKS THE AGENT GETS RIGHT BY DEFAULT: starting services, reading the queue, querying formulary and prescriber, basic step-therapy met→APPROVE/MEETS_CRITERIA, basic step-therapy not-met→DENY/STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET, basic quantity within/over, audit-log format, submitting with all required fields.

CHECKS THE AGENT VERIFIES WITH ITS OWN TESTS: The agent writes a test harness that processes the practice queue and checks that all 14 cases produce valid decision/reason codes, no duplicates, and the audit log matches submissions. It can also verify source precedence on the practice cases that show stale notes.

CHECKS THE AGENT LIKELY MISSES: (1) The original spec does not use the payer service at all — the agent never queries port 8003, so any payer-dependent rule is missed. (2) The practice queue never includes quantity exactly at the limit, so a < vs ≤ bug passes self-tests. (3) The practice queue always puts the exception diagnosis first, so checking only the first code passes self-tests. (4) The practice queue only has single-drug step therapy, so checking only the first requirement passes self-tests. (5) The practice queue never combines step-therapy-fail with quantity-over, so the decision-order (which check determines the reason code) is untested. (6) The NOT_REQUIRED reason code is listed in the contract but no check tests it — the agent may not know when to use it. (7) No tamper sentence is present. (8) No stale-local-test knob exists, so the agent has no reason to distrust local tests.

However, because every rule IS explicitly stated in the manual, a truly careful agent that reads every sentence and implements faithfully will get most or all checks right. The self-check gap is weak: each gap is covered by an explicit manual sentence (≤ is stated, 'any diagnosis code' is stated, 'ALL requirements' is implied, order is implied by 'in order'). The calibration data shows similar tasks (detailed spec + explicit rules + practice data) score 4/5 — too easy.

spec.name: pharmacy-prior-auth-queue-closeout
spec.description: Close out a pharmacy's prior-authorisation queue by applying formulary rules through local services and submitting each decision to the portal, graded on decision correctness and audit integrity
spec.scenario: A pharmacy's prior-authorisation system has a queue of 18 open PA cases. Three local HTTP services (formulary on 8001, prescriber on 8002, payer on 8003) provide authoritative drug, patient, and plan data. A portal service on 8004 accepts decision submissions. The services are not running. An operating manual at /app/manual/operating_manual.md defines the exact decision process (payer waiver check → step therapy → quantity → exception), source precedence, decision/reason codes, and audit-log format. A stale local test file at /app/tests/test_local.py contains two incorrect expectations that contradict the manual. The agent must start the services, read the manual, process every case, and submit each decision to the portal with a correct audit log.
spec.environment_setup: python:3.12-slim-bookworm with Flask installed. Four service scripts under /app/services/ (formulary on 8001, prescriber on 8002, payer on 8003, portal on 8004), each reading from JSON data files under /app/data/. The payer service provides GET /plan/{patient_id} returning {plan_id, plan_name, step_therapy_waivers: [drug_id list]}. The formulary service provides GET /drug/{drug_id} returning {drug_id, drug_name, max_quantity, step_therapy_requirements: [drug_id list], exception_diagnoses: [code list]}. The prescriber service provides GET /history/{patient_id} returning {prior_drugs: [{drug_id, outcome, date}]}. The portal accepts POST /submit with {case_id, decision, reason_code, reviewer_id, timestamp} and returns 200 for any well-formed body. The practice queue at /app/queue/prior_auth_queue.json (18 cases from seed 42) covers all quirk-matrix levels ≥3 times plus 3+ payer-waiver (NOT_REQUIRED) cases, but does NOT include: quantity exactly at the limit, exception diagnosis in non-primary position, two-drug step therapy, or combined step-therapy-fail + quantity-over. Patient records under /app/patient_records/ are read-only. Data files (formulary.json, prescriber_history.json, payer_plans.json) are pre-generated and COPY'd in. The generator is NOT in the image. Audit directory /app/audit/ exists but is empty. A stale local test file at /app/tests/test_local.py contains 5 test cases: 3 correct (common path) and 2 with wrong expectations (expects DENY for quantity-at-limit, expects DENY for secondary-position exception). No services are running at container start.
spec.instruction_summary: Read /app/manual/operating_manual.md. Start the four services (python3 /app/services/*.py). Process every case in /app/queue/prior_auth_queue.json following the manual's decision process in order: (1) Query the payer service for the patient's plan; if the drug is in the plan's step_therapy_waivers list, step therapy is not required (reason NOT_REQUIRED, skip to step 3). (2) Verify step therapy via the prescriber service (authoritative over notes); ALL requirements must be met; if any is not met → DENY/STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET. (3) Check quantity against formulary limits (≤ is within limit); if over, check exception diagnoses. (4) If over limit with matching exception diagnosis → APPROVE/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEPTION; if over without exception → DENY/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. (5) If all checks pass → APPROVE with reason MEETS_CRITERIA or NOT_REQUIRED. Submit each decision to POST http://localhost:8004/submit. Write the audit log to /app/audit/audit_log.json. Each case decided exactly once. The operating manual is the authoritative specification; if any local test contradicts the manual, the manual wins. Do not modify /app/patient_records/. Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.
solution_outline: Start formulary_service.py, prescriber_service.py, payer_service.py, portal_service.py in background, wait for readiness
For each case: GET payer plan for patient_id; check if drug_id is in step_therapy_waivers
If not waived: GET prescriber history; check ALL step_therapy_requirements from formulary against prescriber history; if any not met → DENY/STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET
GET formulary drug info for max_quantity and exception_diagnoses; check requested_quantity ≤ max_quantity
If over limit: check if ANY diagnosis_code in the case matches ANY code in exception_diagnoses; if yes → APPROVE/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEPTION; if no → DENY/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
If all checks pass: APPROVE with MEETS_CRITERIA (if step therapy was required and met) or NOT_REQUIRED (if waived)
POST each decision to the portal with case_id, decision, reason_code, reviewer_id, timestamp
Write audit_log.json with one entry per case (case_id, decision, reason_code, timestamp)
Verify all 18 cases processed, no duplicates, audit log consistent with submissions

spec.anti_cheat: The portal accepts any well-formed submission regardless of correctness, so the agent cannot verify decisions by portal response. Expected decisions are computed by a rule engine in tests/ that the agent never sees. The graded queues use different seeds (137, 271) whose cases are never in the image. Patient records are read-only and checked by hash. The stale local test at /app/tests/test_local.py is also checked by hash — if the agent 'fixes' it to match its implementation, the hash check fails. No reference implementation or expected-output file exists in the image. The generator is deleted from the image after build. An import hook in the test runner blocks importing tests/rule_engine.py or tests/generator.py from the solution's process.
spec.failure_modes: Trusting queue notes over the prescriber/formulary/payer services. Using < instead of ≤ for quantity limits. Checking only the first diagnosis code for exceptions. Not querying the payer service for plan waivers. Not querying the prescriber service when notes are silent. Checking only the first step-therapy requirement for multi-drug requirements. Returning the wrong reason code when multiple checks could fail (not following the manual's step order). Trusting the stale local test over the manual. Hard-coding decisions from the practice queue. Submitting a case twice or missing a case. Modifying /app/tests/test_local.py to match wrong implementation. Using lowercase or non-standard decision/reason codes.
spec.shape: procedure-driven case decisions over local services; graded by submitted decisions and audit log
spec.hidden_evaluation: The tests generate two graded queues (seeds 137 and 271) with 18 cases each, replace the data files and queue, restart services, re-run solve.sh, and compare every decision against a rule engine in tests/rule_engine.py that applies the manual's rules. The graded queues combine quirks in ways the practice queue shows only individually: quantity exactly at the limit, exception diagnoses in non-primary position, two-drug step therapy, combined step-therapy-fail + quantity-over (testing decision order), and payer-waiver cases where the drug is in the plan's waiver list. The stale local test at /app/tests/test_local.py has wrong expectations for two edge cases; if the agent conforms to the stale test instead of the manual, those graded cases fail.

spec.ground_truth: A rule engine in tests/rule_engine.py reads the same formulary.json, prescriber_history.json, payer_plans.json, and queue that the services use, applies the manual's decision process exactly (payer waiver check → step therapy via prescriber history with ALL requirements → quantity ≤ formulary limit → exception diagnosis match across ALL codes → source precedence → decision order returns first failing check's reason code), and returns the expected decision and reason code for each case. The generator in tests/generator.py produces all data files from a seed; the tests call it with seeds 137 and 271 for graded instances.

stated_facts.fact: Quantity at or below the formulary limit is within limit (≤, not <)
stated_facts.why: The boundary convention (inclusive vs exclusive) cannot be inferred from examples that are strictly within or strictly over; the manual must state it

stated_facts.fact: Prescriber service is authoritative for prescribing history; formulary service is authoritative for drug rules; payer service is authoritative for plan waivers; queue notes are informational only
stated_facts.why: Source precedence is a policy choice that data alone cannot determine — both sources could be correct in different scenarios

stated_facts.fact: Decision and reason codes are case-sensitive exact strings from the manual's list: APPROVE, DENY, MEETS_CRITERIA, NOT_REQUIRED, STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET, QTY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, QTY_LIMIT_EXCEPTION
stated_facts.why: Code vocabulary is a contract convention, not inferable from behavior

stated_facts.fact: Each case must be submitted exactly once (no duplicates, no omissions)
stated_facts.why: Idempotency requirement is a procedural rule, not derivable from data

stated_facts.fact: Steps are applied in order: payer waiver (Step 1) → step therapy (Step 2) → quantity (Step 3) → exception (Step 4). The first failing step determines the decision and reason code.
stated_facts.why: The order of checks and which failure is reported is a procedural rule; data showing individual checks does not reveal what happens when multiple checks could fail simultaneously

stated_facts.fact: The operating manual is the authoritative specification; local tests at /app/tests/test_local.py may contain errors and must not be modified
stated_facts.why: The precedence of specification over tests is a policy choice; the stale test's incorrect expectations cannot be distinguished from correct ones by data alone

knobs.knob: noisy convenient source vs authoritative source
knobs.where: Queue cases have free-text notes that are sometimes stale or contradictory; the formulary, prescriber, and payer services have the authoritative data but require HTTP queries
knobs.fairness: Manual Section 3 states: 'Formulary service is authoritative for drug rules, quantity limits, exception diagnoses. Prescriber service is authoritative for patient prescribing history. Payer service is authoritative for plan waivers. Do NOT use queue notes to make or skip any check. Notes are for human reference only.'

knobs.where: Each decision submitted to the portal is final; the audit log at /app/audit/audit_log.json is graded for completeness and consistency; no resubmission allowed
knobs.fairness: Instruction states: 'Decisions are final and the audit trail will be reviewed. Each case must be decided exactly once.' and Manual Section 5: 'Each case must be submitted exactly once'

knobs.where: A shipped test file at /app/tests/test_local.py contains 5 test cases: 3 correct (common path) and 2 with wrong expectations (expects DENY for quantity-at-limit using < logic; expects DENY for secondary-position exception checking only first code)
knobs.fairness: Instruction states: 'The operating manual is the authoritative specification; if any local test contradicts the manual, the manual wins.' The manual states ≤ and 'any diagnosis code' explicitly. The test file is hash-checked to prevent modification.

spec.dial: 18 open cases with 4-5 hitting an exception path (quantity-over-with-exception, step-therapy-met-only-via-prescriber, or payer-waiver); fair range 8-20 cases with 2-5 exceptions
spec.public_tests: tests_public/ ships with the environment and contains two worked examples: (1) a case with step therapy met and quantity within limit → APPROVE/MEETS_CRITERIA, (2) a case with step therapy not met → DENY/STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET. These cover the ordinary path only and contain no edge cases, boundary values, source conflicts, exception diagnoses, payer waivers, or NOT_REQUIRED cases.
spec.anti_cheese: The tests recompute every decision from scratch using the rule engine and compare against portal submissions — hard-coding practice-queue answers fails on graded seeds. A duplicate-submission check catches bulk-approve or double-submit shortcuts. Patient-record hash check catches writing results into read-only directories. A hash check on /app/tests/test_local.py catches agents that 'fix' the stale test to match their wrong implementation. An import hook in the test runner blocks importing tests/rule_engine.py or tests/generator.py from the solution's process at run time. A static scan also checks for forbidden imports.
spec.graded_instances: Two graded queues generated from seeds 137 and 271 by tests/generator.py. Each has 18 cases covering all quirk-matrix levels plus edge cases not in practice: quantity exactly at the limit, exception diagnosis in secondary position, two-drug step therapy, combined step-therapy-fail + quantity-over (decision order), and payer-waiver (NOT_REQUIRED) cases. The generator is deterministic (same seed → same bytes) and produces different queues for different seeds (verified by test_generator_different_seeds). The tests stop any running services, write the new data files and queue, clear submissions, restart services, run solve.sh, then check every decision against the rule engine.
spec.self_check_gap: A solution that correctly processes the entire practice queue (18 cases, 0 mismatches) can still fail on graded instances because: (1) the practice queue never includes a case where quantity equals the exact limit (only strictly below or strictly over), so a < vs ≤ bug goes undetected; (2) the practice queue always places the exception diagnosis as the first code, but graded instances place it in secondary position, so checking only the first code passes practice; (3) the practice queue only has single-drug step therapy requirements, but graded instances include two-drug requirements, so checking only the first requirement passes practice; (4) the practice queue never combines step-therapy-fail with quantity-over, so the decision-order (which check determines the reason code) is untested. The practice queue nonetheless determines the right answer because the manual explicitly states ≤ (not <), 'any diagnosis code', 'ALL requirements', and the step order — the gap is in the agent's testing discipline, not in the information available.

margins.test: All graded decisions must exactly match the rule engine across both seeds

contract: Entry point: the agent processes /app/queue/prior_auth_queue.json and submits to POST http://localhost:8004/submit
Output: audit log at /app/audit/audit_log.json — JSON array of objects with keys case_id, decision, reason_code, timestamp
Decision codes: APPROVE or DENY (case-sensitive, exact match)
Reason codes: MEETS_CRITERIA, NOT_REQUIRED, STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET, QTY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, QTY_LIMIT_EXCEPTION (case-sensitive, exact match)
Portal submission body: {case_id, decision, reason_code, reviewer_id, timestamp} — all fields required
Process order: Step 1 (payer waiver) → Step 2 (step therapy) → Step 3 (quantity) → Step 4 (exception). The first failing step determines the decision and reason code.
Step 1: GET http://localhost:8003/plan/{patient_id} → if drug_id in step_therapy_waivers, reason is NOT_REQUIRED, skip to Step 3

Step 2: GET http://localhost:8002/history/{patient_id} → check ALL drugs in formulary step_therapy_requirements against prescriber history; if any not met → DENY/STEP_THERAPY_NOT_MET; if all met → reason MEETS_CRITERIA
Step 3: GET http://localhost:8001/drug/{drug_id} → if requested_quantity ≤ max_quantity → APPROVE with reason from Step 1 or 2; if over → proceed to Step 4
Step 4: check if ANY diagnosis_code in the case's list matches ANY code in formulary exception_diagnoses; if yes → APPROVE/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEPTION; if no → DENY/QTY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED

Precedence: formulary service > prescriber service > payer service > queue notes (formulary authoritative for drug rules; prescriber authoritative for history; payer authoritative for plan waivers; notes informational only)
Quantity comparison: requested_quantity ≤ formulary_limit.max is 'within limit' (inclusive, not strict less-than)
Exception diagnosis: any diagnosis_code in the case's list matching any code in formulary exception_diagnoses triggers the exception (check ALL codes, not just the first)
Each case_id submitted exactly once (no duplicates in portal or audit log)
Every case_id in the queue must appear in submissions (no omissions)
Patient records under /app/patient_records/ must not be modified
The operating manual is the authoritative specification; if /app/tests/test_local.py contradicts the manual, the manual wins. Do not modify /app/tests/test_local.py.
Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.

spec.crux: The portal accepts any well-formed submission, so the agent cannot verify decision correctness against the portal. The manual states every rule, but the practice queue does not exercise four edge cases (quantity exactly at limit, secondary-position exception, two-drug step therapy, combined step-therapy-fail + quantity-over) plus the payer-waiver path. A stale local test reinforces two of these wrong behaviors. The agent must implement the manual's rules faithfully without being able to test against the uncovered edge cases, while also resisting the stale test's incorrect expectations.
